clue.text: Cycling round the real West End of London? Not Barking (3,5)

indicators.note: the letters of THE REAL go round like a bicycle chain, the last two coming to the front
the cycled word goes round the L, holding it inside
the west end of a word written left to right is its first letter

blocks.note: THE REAL cycled: AL moves from the back to the front
the first letter of London, sitting between AL and THERE

annotation.surface: A cyclist doing laps of the real West End, then a pointed remark about Barking, a borough in east London.
annotation.walkthrough: Barking is an east London district, so the surface pairs it with the West End; here it is slang for mad, and 'not barking' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone with all their wits about them is sane, the opposite of barking mad.

clue.text: Wingless insects remain in a state of inactivity (3)

definitions.text: remain in a state of inactivity

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its two outer letters, so they are cut off

blocks.note: flies are insects
FLIES without its outer letters F and S

annotation.surface: Insects without wings, left sitting about doing nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes wingless literal, since a flightless insect has little choice but to stay put; in the wordplay the wings are the end letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in land left to lie fallow or money lying idle.

clue.text: Verity gets tense sitting next to David's great-grandmother (5)

indicators.note: one piece sits right beside the other, so the two are simply joined

blocks.note: t = tense, the grammar abbreviation
in the Bible, Ruth is the great-grandmother of King David

annotation.surface: A woman called Verity getting nervous beside an elderly relative of someone called David.
annotation.walkthrough: Verity reads as a woman's name, but here it is the plain noun. The Book of Ruth ends with her family line down to David.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal synonym from Latin veritas, as in 'the eternal verities'.

clue.text: The best placed card player from Athens led off with diamonds (6,4)

indicators.note: off means gone bad, so the letters of ATHENS LED are rearranged
with means accompanied by, so D is added after the rearranged letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, nine letters
d = diamonds, the card suit abbreviation

annotation.surface: A Greek card player takes the lead with a diamond and turns out to be the strongest at the table.
annotation.walkthrough: Led looks like card play, but it is fodder; off is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A card-game term for the player on the dealer's left, who leads first and so holds the best position in games like piquet.

clue.text: Former model making out (6)

blocks.note: ex = former, as in ex-wife
to model for an artist is to pose

annotation.surface: An ex-model caught making out with someone.
annotation.walkthrough: Making out suggests a kiss; here out is a verb, and making joins wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Out as a verb means to reveal someone's secret, typically their sexuality, publicly.

clue.text: Papers kept in small trophy somewhere in London (6)

indicators.note: something kept in a box is held inside it, so ID goes inside S + CUP

blocks.note: s = small, as on clothing labels
a cup is a trophy
identity papers are your ID; it goes between S and CUP

annotation.surface: Documents tucked inside a little trophy cup.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is deliberately vague, so the wordplay has to do the work.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this suburb lies in the London borough of Bexley, in the south-east of the city.

clue.text: Pornographic material is mounted at prime locations (4)

indicators.note: prime means prime number, so take the letters in positions 2, 3, 5 and 7

blocks.note: count along ISMOUNTED and keep positions 2, 3, 5 and 7

annotation.surface: Pornography being put up in the best spots, like posters.
annotation.walkthrough: Prime here means prime numbers, not the best places the surface suggests; it is a rare device, so counting is the only way in.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word for indecent writing or pictures, with a sense of dirt from its original meaning of a sooty mark.

clue.text: Dark humour spread thick (3-6)

blocks.note: a dim room is dark
wit is humour
to ted is to spread hay out to dry

annotation.surface: Black comedy laid on with a trowel.
annotation.walkthrough: Spread thick looks like a phrase, but spread gives TED and thick stands alone as the definition. Ted, meaning to toss new-mown hay, is a farming word.
annotation.definitionFit: Thick is informal for stupid, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Mad, mad ruler, not very progressive (11)

indicators.note: mad means crazy, so the letters that follow go wild

blocks.note: anagram fodder, eleven letters

annotation.surface: A deranged king who is anything but forward-thinking.
annotation.walkthrough: Mad appears twice: the first is the instruction and the second is part of the fodder. Not very progressive reads as one phrase, but not belongs to the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Ultra- means extremely, so the word is literally very modern, and modern stands for progressive.

clue.text: Maybe hiding from danger underground (6)

indicators.note: the answer is taken from inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap: danGER UNDerground

annotation.surface: Taking shelter below ground from some threat.
annotation.walkthrough: Hiding looks like a verb in the surface, but it is a word being named, and maybe flags it as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: in 'hiding is useless', hiding is a verb form used as a noun, which is what the grammar term names.

clue.text: Professor suspected of murder seen at opera house before darkness finally falls (8)

indicators.note: before means earlier in line, so MET is placed ahead of S
finally points to the end of the word it follows, its last letter

blocks.note: Professor Plum is a suspect in the board game Cluedo (Clue in North America)
the Met is the Metropolitan Opera in New York
the last letter of darkness

annotation.surface: A murder suspect spotted at the opera just before nightfall, like a scene from a whodunit.
annotation.walkthrough: Falls looks like the end of the scene, darkness falling, but it is the definition, and darkness only lends its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with extra force: to plummet is to fall straight down, fast.

clue.text: Stressed MP? Ease his stress (9)

indicators.note: under strain, the letters that follow are bent out of shape

blocks.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

annotation.surface: A harried Member of Parliament, and a call to calm them down.
annotation.walkthrough: Stress appears at both ends in two senses: the first means strain and tells you to rearrange, the last means put weight on and is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to stress a point is to give it weight.

clue.text: Out of energy, remain strong when waving red rag (7,4)

indicators.note: out of means lacking, so E, for energy, is taken out
the remaining letters wave about into a new order

blocks.note: e = energy, as in E = mc²
REMAIN STRONG less its E, eleven letters of anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A bullfighter, exhausted, trying to stand firm while flourishing the red cape.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is the bullring, but a rag is slang for a newspaper and red means communist.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: Britain's socialist daily paper, long associated with the Communist Party, is fairly called a red rag.

clue.text: Ethiopian princess who dies in city square after being flayed (4)

indicators.note: flaying strips the skin, so the outer letters go

blocks.note: a maidan is an open square in a city, as in Kyiv's Maidan
MAIDAN without its outer letters M and N

annotation.surface: A grisly execution: a princess skinned and killed in a public square.
annotation.walkthrough: The city square is a maidan, a word from Persian used in South Asia and Ukraine.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the title heroine of Verdi's opera is an Ethiopian princess who dies sealed in a tomb with Radamès.

clue.text: Theatrical chap provides accommodation for young man in 24 (10)

indicators.note: a host who provides accommodation has the guest inside, so MAN holds BOY
in means inside, so the result goes inside FLAT

blocks.note: the answer to 24 down
a chap is a man
a boy is a young man; M(BOY)AN then sits inside FLA…T

annotation.surface: An actor lets a young lodger stay in his flat.
annotation.walkthrough: Theatrical looks like it describes the chap, but it stands alone as the definition. A number in a clue stands for the answer at that number.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe showy, dramatic behaviour.

clue.text: Spent hours collecting good preliminary sketches (6)

indicators.note: spent means worn out, so the letters of HOURS are rearranged
the rearranged letters gather G inside them

blocks.note: HOURS rearranged
g = good; it goes between ROU and HS

annotation.surface: An artist who has spent hours getting some decent early drafts together.
annotation.walkthrough: Spent hours reads as time passing, but spent is the instruction to rearrange HOURS.
annotation.definitionFit: A design-studio term: rough versions of a drawing or layout made before the finished art.

clue.text: European articles give greater strength to this suggestion (9)

blocks.note: UN is French for a, and DER is German for the
to tone muscles is to firm and strengthen them

annotation.surface: A proposal that European articles, perhaps of a treaty, should be made stronger.
annotation.walkthrough: European articles means grammar articles from two languages, not clauses of a treaty.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of a hint: an underlying feeling felt beneath what is said.

clue.text: Wasted time in British Library with old religious texts from the east (6)

indicators.note: in means inside, so T is placed inside the rest
with means alongside, so BL and O join the reversed texts
read from the east, that is right to left in an across clue, so OT becomes TO

blocks.note: BL is the British Library's abbreviation
o = old
OT, the Old Testament, reversed
t = time; it goes between BLO and TO

annotation.surface: A scholar who has frittered away time in the British Library over ancient Eastern scriptures.
annotation.walkthrough: Wasted time reads as idle hours, but wasted alone is the definition. From the east reverses because across answers read west to east.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for very drunk, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Place an order for tinned nuts (6)

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of TINNED go wild

blocks.note: anagram fodder, six letters

annotation.surface: Ordering a can of nuts.
annotation.walkthrough: Tinned nuts looks like a grocery item; nuts is the anagram instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A British business and military term: to indent for supplies is to requisition them with an official order.

clue.text: Mark made by industrial waste, making large mark (6)

indicators.note: making X into Y turns one thing into another, so the L of large becomes the M of mark

blocks.note: sludge is industrial waste
l = large is swapped for m = mark, the old German currency

annotation.surface: A stain left by factory effluent that spreads into a big blot.
annotation.walkthrough: Mark appears twice: the first is the definition, the second is the currency.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a dirty, blurred mark, the sort sludge would leave.

clue.text: Second century Semite amulet (6)

blocks.note: s = second
c = century, as in cricket scores
Arabs are a Semitic people

annotation.surface: An ancient lucky charm from the second century AD belonging to a Semitic people.
annotation.walkthrough: Second century reads as a date, but it is two abbreviations.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the ancient Egyptians carved beetle-shaped charms as protection.

clue.text: Harmful organism concealed by fingermark (4)

indicators.note: the answer is concealed inside the next word

blocks.note: sits in the middle: finGERMark

annotation.surface: Bacteria lurking in a fingerprint, as a forensic lab might warn.
annotation.walkthrough: It is apt, since fingermarks really do carry microbes.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain definition: the everyday word for a microbe that causes disease.

clue.text: Escort business used by a Conservative (9)

indicators.note: used by means taken up by, so A and C take COMPANY after them

blocks.note: the a is kept as it stands
C = Conservative, the British political party
a company is a business

annotation.surface: A Tory politician caught using an escort agency.
annotation.walkthrough: Escort business suggests an agency, but escort alone is the verb definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to go along with someone.

clue.text: Romp on a beach in Ibiza? (5)

indicators.note: on means on top of, and in a down clue that puts PLAY above A

blocks.note: to romp is to play boisterously
the a is kept as it stands

annotation.surface: A frolic on a Spanish holiday beach.
annotation.walkthrough: Ibiza is a Spanish island, and the question mark flags that the definition wants the Spanish word.
annotation.definitionFit: A foreign-language definition: the Spanish word for beach, seen on Ibiza's signposts.

clue.text: Note pad (4)

blocks.note: a musical note lowered by a semitone, written ♭
pad is slang for home, here an apartment

annotation.walkthrough: Note pad reads as stationery; split it into two words, each a separate meaning.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a note lowered a semitone, as in B flat, and a British apartment, which slang calls a pad.

clue.text: Posh car follows street walker (8)

indicators.note: follows means comes after, so ROLLER is placed after ST

blocks.note: St = street, as in addresses
a Roller is British slang for a Rolls-Royce

annotation.surface: A kerb-crawler in a luxury car trailing a prostitute.
annotation.walkthrough: Street walker is a phrase for a prostitute, but street gives ST and walker is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who strolls is a leisurely walker.

clue.text: Tree found in areas full of prickly plants after temperature's dropped (6)

indicators.note: full of means holding inside, so A A is filled with the cacti
dropped means let go, so T, for temperature, is removed from CACTI

blocks.note: a = area, twice
cacti are prickly plants
CACTI loses T, for temperature, and sits inside A…A

annotation.surface: A tree that grows among cacti once the heat has gone out of the day.
annotation.walkthrough: Areas is plural so it gives two As, which wrap round what is left of the cacti.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the thorny wattle tree of dry lands.

clue.text: Passion leads to intimate relations and unlimited sex (3)

indicators.note: the leads of words are their front letters, so take the first letters of intimate relations
sex without its limits, its outer letters, leaves the middle

blocks.note: the first letters of intimate and relations
the middle letter of sex

annotation.surface: Passion leading to a love affair and no-holds-barred sex.
annotation.walkthrough: The passion of the surface is desire; the definition's passion is anger.
annotation.definitionFit: Passion in the older sense of a fit of strong feeling, here rage.

clue.text: East side of Leyton (6)

blocks.note: an old name for the lands of the East, from Latin for rising
a side is a team; Leyton's football club is in east London

annotation.surface: The eastern edge of Leyton, a district of east London.
annotation.walkthrough: Side means a team, not an edge: Leyton Orient is a professional football club based in Leyton.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the old word for the East, where the sun rises, and the second half of the Leyton club's name.

clue.text: Cross-eyed brat thrown under the bus (8)

indicators.note: cross means angry, and the letters that follow are in a temper and out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, eight letters

annotation.surface: A squinting child shoved in front of a bus.
annotation.walkthrough: Cross-eyed reads as one word, but the hyphen hides a split: cross is the instruction and eyed brat the fodder. Thrown reads like the anagram signal but belongs to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to throw someone under the bus is to sacrifice them for your own gain.
